name: Rory Stewart
role: British Conservative MP (2010-2019), Minister of State, Prisons Minister and International Development Secretary
summary: A Conservative MP who wrote and spoke mainly on foreign policy, intervention and constitutional questions. He favours localism and caution about foreign interventions, and supports NATO and Trident. He voted with the party on most economic and social questions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: TheyWorkForYou reports he generally voted for same-sex marriage (3 for, 3 absent).

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Reported to have voted for replacing Trident; the vote record is used.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Reported to have voted for mass surveillance and communications data retention.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Reported to have voted against a lower voting age (3 against).

proportional-representation.rationale: Reported to have generally voted against a more proportional system.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Reported to have voted for more restrictive regulation of trade union activity (9 for).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reported to have voted against a higher income-tax rate over 150,000, a mansion tax and higher capital gains tax.

free-public-college.rationale: Reported to have voted for university tuition fees.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Reported to have voted against measures to prevent climate change (6 against, 1 for, 8 absent); thin, reported record only.

second-chamber.rationale: Argued in the Commons for keeping an unelected second chamber valued for the expertise of its members, against elected senators.

direct-votes.rationale: Argued that constitutional change should need a referendum or super-majority; that covers constitutional laws, not major laws generally.

democracy-best.rationale: Said 'Democracy is and must remain the answer' and called it a moral value resting on equal human dignity.

universal-morality.rationale: Said human rights are universal and inviolable and that democratic values are universal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said democracy rests on the equality and dignity of humans and that human rights are universal and inviolable.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Said the ECHR is unambiguous on torture; even a hypothetical ticking-bomb case should be prosecuted, so torture stays illegal.

decide-locally.rationale: Argued that communities know and care more than distant officials and should do more, while saying the state is still needed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Said Britain has a moral right and duty to impose a no-fly zone in Libya and supported Resolution 1973, while urging caution.

non-intervention.rationale: Said Britain has a moral right and duty to act against Gaddafi's attack on his own people.

force-without-un.rationale: Endorsed the position that Britain has a moral right to act but will not do so without UN backing.

collective-defense.rationale: Argued Britain must make NATO's article 5 defence credible, including readiness to use nuclear weapons for a NATO member.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Argued for a credible British commitment under NATO's article 5.

rehabilitation.rationale: As Prisons Minister he led a policy against very short sentences because they reoffend more; ministerial policy rather than his own words.

citizens-assembly.rationale: As leadership candidate proposed a 'Brexit Assembly', a grand jury of citizens, to break the deadlock.

notes: Most speeches 2016-2019 were ministerial and state government policy, so they are not used as his own views except the prison policy he led (low). Themes searched: defence, intervention, constitution, localism, prisons, democracy, human rights, taxes and welfare (votes only); economy, society, ecology and technology are thin. TheyWorkForYou aggregates are a secondhand report of votes and are capped at medium.
